generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL. PK boundary literals from the atomic summary are honoured by the compact DB rows, not by generated rows (generated PKs are fresh sequential values that do not collide with compact max).
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent key value; allow NULL only where the column is nullable; include parent rows without children and child rows with NULL FK. FK boundary literals are honoured by compact DB rows; generated FKs reference generated or compact parent keys.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_quantity: Positive integers sampled from a small range (1..500) unless a per-column exception gives bounds.
generic_sampling_rules.real_price: Non-negative REAL rounded to 2 decimals, sampled from 0.0..100.0; NULL share per column statistics.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Short title-case strings; include near-variants (case changes, trailing punctuation) and duplicates on DISTINCT columns.
generic_sampling_rules.text_long: Sentence-like strings up to 200 chars; may be empty string or NULL where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_uuid: Lowercase UUID-like hex string; include uppercase near-variants.
generic_sampling_rules.date_iso: Dates in %Y-%m-%d between 1850-01-01 and 2015-12-31; include boundary values at listed literals and one day on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.text_timestamp: Timestamps formatted 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC' between 2011-01-01 and 2012-12-31.
generic_sampling_rules.null_rule: Every nullable column gets at least one NULL row and at least one non-NULL row per instance; NULL share follows the compact database share; planted NULLs are never replaced. Columns that are 100% NULL in the compact DB (Dish.description, Menu.keywords, Menu.language, Menu.location_type) are generated NULL-dominant with a small positive non-NULL share (at least one non-NULL row per instance). Columns not listed in null_targets are generated non-NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_rule: For each atomic-operation literal on a non-key column, include the literal, one step below and one step above (numbers by step 1 or 0.01, dates by one day). Boundary literals on PK/FK columns are satisfied by compact DB rows; generated PK/FK values are fresh and do not collide.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_rule: For ORDER BY ... LIMIT columns, plant at least two rows tied at the listed rank.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_rule: For DISTINCT columns, plant duplicate values covering 20-50% of rows; boundary literals are reserved before duplicate sampling so they survive.
generic_sampling_rules.group_distinct_rule: For columns with rows_with_different_values pattern, ensure each FK group with >=2 children has at least two distinct non-NULL values.

issues.evidence: spec.BOUNDARY places boundary literals on primary-key and foreign-key columns: ('Dish','id'):[106,107,108], ('Menu','id'):[12463,...], ('MenuPage','id'):[143,144,145,1388,1389,1390], ('MenuPage','menu_id'):[12881,12882,12883], ('MenuItem','menu_page_id'):[143,144,145,1388,1389,1390]. These literal sets were harvested from query predicates (comparison_boundary targets) which is correct for separating query denotations, but in instance.py build_random_instance the integer PK is overwritten by _next_pk (sequential max+1) AFTER samplers run, and FK values are overwritten by fill_foreign_keys_consistently AFTER _plant_boundaries. Consequently, boundary literal sets on PK/FK columns are never realized as row values. This is fine for FK because it must remain referentially valid; but the spec's PARENT_WITHOUT_CHILDREN targeting MenuPage.id=144 / Menu.id=12882 etc. is provided as literal values only. _ensure_unmatched detaches NULL wherever no free parent exists, but does not ensure the specific boundary PKs (144, 1388, 12882, 12463...) are actually reachable and matchable against generated parent rows. Because compact DB already holds those PKs, they remain matchable, so denotation-separation on these literals depends entirely on compact rows, not on generated construction. Request: (a) clarify in the spec that PK/FK boundary literals are honoured by the compact DB and not generated, and (b) generate some MenuPage.id / Menu.id rows with values not colliding with compact max, ensuring at least one generated parent row with the boundary id exists so the query can find a generated boundary row — or explicitly state why relying on compact rows is acceptable.
issues.requested_revision: Add a spec clarification for PK/FK boundary literals (or generate a boundary PK on a non-colliding table when feasible), so that literal pools are not silently dropped.

issues.evidence: spec.BOUNDARY for ('MenuItem','price') TIE_COLUMNS targets ('MenuItem','price') with 'tie_at_rank':[1] DESC, but spec.py only lists ('MenuItem','price') under TIE_COLUMNS and _plant_ties runs BEFORE _fix_formulas and BEFORE null planting? Actually order is _plant_nulls first, then _plant_boundaries, then _plant_duplicates, then _plant_ties, then _fix_formulas. Ties set the top two values to max(remaining non-nulls). Then _fix_formulas may clamp negative prices to 0, but only if price<0, which won't happen. However, the group semantics requested 'rows_with_different_values: >=2 per group with different values' — this is not implemented anywhere. The pattern rows_with_different_values (per MenuPage group with different prices) is not enforced by construction. Ties are planted but the 'at least 2 different values per group' invariant is only satisfied by chance (sampling from uniform pool). Execution feedback does not confirm separation of the 'ties_for_order_limit' or 'rows_with_different_values' targets for MenuItem.price. No evidence exists that grouped-by-page rows have >=2 different prices. Request: verify by construction (or state explicitly) that each MenuItem.menu_page_id group has at least two rows with distinct price values.
issues.requested_revision: Add a construction step that guarantees per-FK-group distinct-value coverage on MenuItem.price for groups that have >=2 children.

issues.evidence: Specification NULL rule (interface rule 7) requires that for every nullable column each instance contains generated rows with NULL AND rows with non-NULL. But spec.NULL_SHARE and NULL_DOMINANT cause some columns to have NULL share 1.0 (Dish.description, Menu.keywords, Menu.language, Menu.location_type), which yields zero non-NULL rows in any instance — see execution feedback: 'Dish.description: NULL 3766 / 3766', 'Menu.keywords: NULL 1863/1863', 'Menu.language: 1863/1863', 'Menu.location_type: 1863/1863'. These are all-'NULL-0 non-NULL', which violates the interface rule 'each instance contains generated rows with NULL and rows with non-NULL values'. The spec text off-spec: 'Dish.description, Menu.keywords, Menu.language and Menu.location_type are 100% NULL in the sample; they are generated as NULL-dominant.' The interface explicitly forbids all-NULL columns. Request: update the NULL rule so every nullable column has at least one non-NULL generated value per instance, mapping 100% NULL columns to a small positive non-NULL share.
issues.requested_revision: Set a fixed low non-NULL probability for NULL_DOMINANT columns (e.g., one planted non-NULL row per instance) to comply with rule 7.

issues.evidence: Code in instance.py _plant_nulls: shares of 1.0 for NULL_DOMINANT columns (spec.NULL_DOMINANT includes Dish.description, Menu.keywords, Menu.language, Menu.location_type) plant all-NULL, matching the ALL-NULL execution evidence. Also observe NULL execution on non-null-constraint columns: 'Dish.first_appeared: NULL 20/3766', 'Dish.menus_appeared: NULL 20/3766', 'MenuItem.created_at: NULL 20/7902', 'Menu.dish_count: NULL 15/1863', 'Menu.status: NULL 17/1863', 'Menu.location: NULL 19/1863', 'MenuPage.image_id: NULL 17/3471', 'MenuPage.menu_id: NULL 19/3471'. Dish/menu columns like first_appeared, menus_appeared are NOT nullable in the compact DB per the column-statistics evidence (no default null evidence). Menu.dish_count, Menu.status, Menu.location, MenuPage.image_id are similarly not enumerated under null_targets in the specification, yet the NULL rule in instance.py iterates over all columns with cm.notnull == False. The spec's null_targets list is narrower than what the program NULLs. Request: restrict _plant_nulls to the columns listed in null_targets (or extend null_targets with evidence) so that NULL share matches compact-DB nullability, and ensure columns outside null_targets keep nullable-only when the compact DB has NULLs.
issues.requested_revision: Gate _plant_nulls on (t,c) in null_targets, or add the missing columns to null_targets after verifying compact-DB NULL evidence.

issues.evidence: instance.py _plant_duplicates only handles ('Dish','name'). But spec's duplicate_share '20-50 %' is provided for Dish.name only; no other DISTINCT column is present in DUPLICATE_COLUMNS. This matches the spec, so acceptable. However, Dish.name is a nullable-string primary deduplication column: after _plant_duplicates, _plant_boundaries is already run BEFORE _plant_duplicates (they set boundary case variants and then overwrite some with duplicates). Because both _plant_boundaries and _plant_duplicates overwrite values, the boundary variants 'Clear green turtle' / 'clear green turtle' may be eliminated — duplicates overwrite by sampling from existing non-NULL values, so at least any planted boundary literals present can be selected, but coverage is not guaranteed. Execution feedback does not confirm Dish.name boundaries appear in generated rows. Request: verify (a) outer-vs-new boundaries survive duplicate over-write for Dish.name, and (b) if not, adjust ordering to run duplicates first, boundaries second.
issues.requested_revision: Reserve boundary literals for Dish.name before duplicates sampling (swap order or exclude rows that hold boundary values from being overwritten).

issues.evidence: In instance.py build_random_instance, after fill_foreign_keys_consistently copies FK values from parents, sample_fresh_primary_keys and drop_unique_duplicates are applied. drop_unique_duplicates removes rows to make UNIQUE columns distinct — for Menu, MenuPage, Dish (only id is PK) it never fires. However, after filter, FK consistency may be broken: '_filter(cols, keep)' drops rows, which is fine because FKs were already assigned. Then fill loop: 'if pt == t' reassigns children of the same table (self-FK) to values existing in the filtered set — safe. No block.

choose_table_sizes uses base + rng.randint(-40, 40) despite spec comment claiming 0-230. Average matches spec sizes plus small jitter — the spec pins exact sizes {Dish:200, Menu:120, MenuPage:180, MenuItem:400}, but ±40 variance changes them. Execution shows Dish 3826/20 ≈ 191, Menu 1863/20 ≈ 93 (well below 120), MenuPage 3471/20 ≈ 174, MenuItem 7902/20 ≈ 395. Menu is 93, notably well below the base 120, because 26 of 120 rows were dropped per instance (probably from _ensure_unmatched detach, or drop_unique_duplicates on unique FK). The intended 120 base for Menu is not honoured. Request: either state that sizes are approximate, or remove the ±40 variance to keep exact counts.
issues.requested_revision: Honour TABLE_SIZES exactly per spec, or document approximate sizing in the spec.
